methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective two-center design with an independent external validation cohort (177 + 83) is appropriate for a radiomics prediction task, and the authors apply reasonable preprocessing (ICC>0.75 feature filtering, resampling to 1x1x1 mm3, gray-level discretization) and multi-step feature selection (mRMR then LASSO with 10-fold CV). However, no a priori sample-size/power calculation is reported, the initial feature-to-event ratio is very unfavorable (2,264 features vs ~79 IAC events), and ROI segmentation was ultimately confirmed by a single radiologist with reproducibility checked on only 30 of 260 cases. Statistically, performance is adequately summarized (AUC with 95% CI, DeLong test, DCA, calibration, 5-fold CV), but no correction for multiplicity across feature screening is described, handling of missing data is not stated, and clinical variables were explicitly excluded, limiting benchmark comparison against a clinical-only model.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study developing and externally validating a diagnostic prediction model (Oxford 2b). The clinical question — distinguishing invasive from pre/minimally invasive adenocarcinoma in subcentimeter subsolid nodules — is genuinely important for surgical planning versus active surveillance. External AUC of 0.778 (95% CI 0.673-0.862) with balanced sensitivity/specificity (~72-74%) is encouraging but not practice-changing, and the model is not yet linked to patient-centered endpoints (OS/PFS) or integrated with clinical variables, so translational value is plausible but preliminary.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the appropriate standard for a diagnostic prediction model; the authors instead cite RQS (Supplementary Table 1). Core TRIPOD items are mostly addressed: participant flow (Figure 1), predictors, model development, internal and external validation, calibration, DCA, and limitations. Gaps include no explicit TRIPOD checklist, no reporting of missing data handling, incomplete clinical baseline reporting (e.g., mean age given but smoking status, nodule size distribution underreported in text), and no model equation/intercept or publicly available risk calculator. No data or code sharing statement is present in the blinded text, and the radiomics platform is proprietary (uAI Research Portal) — reproducibility is therefore limited.

novelty_literature.justification: The work is incremental. Radiomics-ML prediction of invasiveness in subsolid lung nodules with SHAP interpretability has been published repeatedly (the authors themselves cite directly comparable Zuo et al. and Li et al. studies in part-solid adenocarcinoma, and acknowledge concordance of their top predictors with those works). The main differentiators are the restriction to subcentimeter SSNs (≤1 cm) and inclusion of an external cohort scanned on matched hardware; neither constitutes a new method, mechanism, or paradigm. SHAP is now standard practice rather than a novel contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable and well-structured (background → workflow → results → biologically-grounded SHAP discussion). However, there is noticeable duplication (the uAI Research Portal/PyRadiomics/IBSI paragraph is repeated verbatim within Methods), limitations contain two bullets labeled 'Third', figure numbering in the abstract/results doesn't fully align with the listed captions (e.g., SHAP described as Figure 9 in text but Figure 8 in caption list), and the abstract conflates feature names (wavelet_HLL_glszm_LowGrayLevelZoneEmphasis vs wavelet_glszm_wavelet.HLL... in results). Captions are informative but some tables (RQS, confusion matrices) are only referenced through supplements.

key_strengths: Independent external validation cohort scanned on matched CT platforms, with AUC 0.778 (95% CI 0.673-0.862) supporting cross-institutional generalizability
Multi-step, reproducibility-aware feature pipeline (ICC>0.75, mRMR, LASSO with 10-fold CV) and transparent comparison of three classifiers with DeLong tests
SHAP-based global and local interpretability with biologically plausible narrative linking top features to necrosis, morphologic irregularity, and air-trapping
Clinical utility assessed with calibration, PRC and DCA in both internal and external cohorts
key_concerns: Small training set (n=123) relative to 2,264 initial features and only ~79 IAC events overall; no a priori power/sample-size calculation and no multiplicity correction beyond LASSO
Highly incremental novelty — directly comparable prior radiomics-SHAP models in subsolid LUAD (Zuo et al., Li et al.) are acknowledged by the authors with concordant findings
TRIPOD not explicitly followed, missing data handling unreported, no public data/code or model equation; proprietary uAI Research Portal limits independent replication
Clinical and semantic radiological features deliberately excluded, so added value of the radiomic model over a simple clinical-radiologic baseline is not demonstrated
Editorial issues: duplicated Methods paragraph, two 'Third' bullets in limitations, abstract-vs-results figure numbering and feature-name inconsistencies
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent but highly incremental external-validation radiomics study with modest sample size, limited novelty, and no code/data sharing; it fits a Tier 4 oncology outlet with minor revisions to tighten TRIPOD reporting, resolve textual inconsistencies, and benchmark against a clinical-only comparator.
